critical_guards: Do not silently normalize the St Andrews catalogue transcription 'Panis' to 'Penis'. The historical price-list row reads Penis; the object catalogue reads Panis. Preserve both source states.

Catalogue no. 383 is a product/offering address, not a unique physical serial number. Closing the offering identity does not establish which production batch or shipment produced the surviving St Andrews slide.
Do not infer Fritz Meyer personally prepared BPM/1/T8/6 merely because he directed/organized the Naples preparation department.
Do not assign a price until the page/table columns are visually checked; row text identity is independent of unresolved price alignment.
research_payoff: This is the first strong surviving-object ↔ exact Naples catalogue-offering closure in the St Andrews group. The slide carries a catalogue-like product address through institutional dispersal: the same taxon and number survive alongside Naples labels, while later St Andrews storage adds further addresses. It upgrades the Naples case from catalogue → British shipment plus separate surviving group to a direct catalogue offering → surviving institutional object relation, without conflating offering identity with individual-copy provenance.
next: No further web search is needed for row 383. Only inspect the slide image if resolving the Panis/Penis handwriting matters to a publication claim, or a page image if row-383 price is required.
